options.text: Multiplying each frequency by the class width
Adding a running total of the frequencies
Dividing each frequency by the total
Subtracting each frequency from the total

questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency is a running total: each value is the sum of all frequencies up to and including that class.

questions.stem: On a cumulative frequency graph, the median is found at:

options.text: The midpoint of the $x$-axis
Where the curve is steepest
The highest point on the curve
The $\frac{n}{2}$ position on the cumulative frequency axis

questions.explanation: Read across from the $\frac{n}{2}$ value on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then down to the $x$-axis to find the median.

options.text: The range divided by 4

questions.explanation: The IQR $= Q_3 - Q_1$, which measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

questions.stem: For a dataset of 60 items, the lower quartile ($Q_1$) is found at the cumulative frequency value of:
On a cumulative frequency graph, the points should be plotted at:

options.text: Any point within the class
The lower boundary of each class
The midpoint of each class
The upper boundary of each class

questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency points are plotted at the upper boundary of each class, because the cumulative frequency tells us how many values are less than that boundary.

questions.stem: Why is the IQR often preferred over the range?

options.text: Because it always equals the median
Because it is easier to calculate
Because it is not affected by extreme values (outliers)
Because it uses all the data values

questions.explanation: The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of data, ignoring extreme values at both ends. This makes it resistant to outliers.

questions.stem: The last point on a cumulative frequency curve should have a cumulative frequency equal to:

options.text: The total frequency $n$
The number of classes
The median

questions.explanation: The final cumulative frequency value must equal the total number of data items ($n$), since all values have been counted.
